summary: The figure is tiny and flips from upright to horizontal in about four frames right after the cut, and the shot's standoff idea (two figures, a world in each hand) is not visible.

faults.what: Right after the cut the figure goes from upright (138.56) to tilted (138.63), then fully horizontal and curled (138.69). That is a fast rotation over about 4 frames, so the cut is tweening into the pose. It reads as a snap or tumble, not a held shot.
faults.fix: Start the shot already on the horizontal pose, or hold the upright pose and cut so no rotation shows in frames 1-6.

faults.what: The shot should show two figures face to face, each with a world in hand, in a standoff. Only one tiny figure is visible, drifting alone in the starfield, with no second character and no props or worlds in its hands.
faults.fix: Frame both characters facing each other with the props visible, or check that the correct camera and shot are playing.

faults.what: The subject is only a few pixels tall and its silhouette is lost among the stars. The planet at lower left pulls the eye, and the figure stays small and unclear throughout the strip.
faults.fix: Move the camera in or scale the figure up so the pose reads as the main subject, and keep the planet out of the focal area.

faults.what: The body is a flat horizontal clump with no clear line of action or visible arms winding up. It does not read as a wind-up or as holding anything.
faults.fix: Use a clearer wind-up silhouette with open arms and the props visible.
